answer: A human-backed agent registry shares one daily admission across its tide forecasting, nebula imaging and whisper transcription queues. Each applicant proves possession of a personhood credential and derives a daily nullifier from its secret; the verifier rejects any nullifier already used in any of the three queues. One person can therefore admit only 1 agent per day, even with many account keys. Extra aliases need separately verified humans. This requires an issuer that prevents duplicate enrollment; rented credentials remain a weakness.
